As already noted earlier (in our chapter on the hardness of interactive proofs), given an honest prover $\Pi$, it is essentially impossible for a malicious prover $\hat{\pi}$ to cheat on this game (because there may not even be any witness that $\Pi$ actually computes $\Pi(\lambda)$ ).
In case $\Pi$'s computation has some complexity that allows us to perform certain polynomial computations (using only linear number of steps), $\Pi$ can try to "hack" the game by performing polynomially-many extra steps during the communication phase (the game proceeds by first taking $\Pi(\epsilon)$ as input $\pi$ and then deriving $\pi'$ from $\pi$ by performing one of these polynomially-many arbitrary extra steps).
